reasoning: The existing skill already covers exact answer selection and concise canonical formatting, so no duplicative rules are needed. Preserve the distinct guidance for bare-list prompts, acronym expansions, and reversing verbal wordplay to recover an intended phrase. These edits target separate locations.

edits.content:
### Intended phrases in verbal wordplay
When a clue gives a distorted or transformed expression (such as a spoonerism) and asks what was meant, reverse the transformation and return the intended phrase. Do not substitute the altered wording, a longer anecdotal quotation, or another example of the same wordplay.

- When a prompt consists only of a pair or list of names, do not assume it asks for the relationship among them. Check the context for the salient shared association the prompt is likely eliciting—such as a country, place, organization, work, or category—and return that shared entity when best supported. Give a relationship only when the wording asks how the entities are related.

edits.target: - Use complementary passages to confirm or disambiguate an answer when helpful. Follow the requested format and retain any qualifiers necessary to the answer.
edits.content: - When a clue asks what an acronym or initialism stands for, or asks what feature it names, give its spelled-out canonical expansion rather than repeating the abbreviation. Use the abbreviation itself only when it is the requested answer.
